answer:
Accept draft token x with min(1,p(x)/q(x)). On rejection, sample from normalized max(p−q,0), then stop verifying that block because later target rows used the rejected prefix. If all K proposals pass, sample a bonus token from the target distribution at the full prefix. The accepted contribution min(p,q) plus the residual max(p−q,0) recovers p. Identical tokenizer/vocabulary and correctly conditioned probabilities are necessary.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For one draft draw, accepted probability mass at token $x$ is $q(x)\min(1,p(x)/q(x))=\min(p(x),q(x))$. The residual mass is $(p(x)-q(x))_+$. Their sum is exactly $p(x)$, establishing correctness when the proposal and target probabilities correspond to the same prefix and vocabulary. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://jaykmody.com/blog/speculative-sampling/) and [2](https://research.google/blog/looking-back-at-speculative-decoding/).
